text: Vigorous writing is concise. A sentence should contain no unnecessary words, a paragraph no unnecessary sentences, for the same reason that a drawing should have no unnecessary lines and a machine no unnecessary parts.
teaches: Every word has a job; cut the ones that do none.
avoid: The run of parallel clauses as a flourish. In a short email, one plain statement of the rule is enough.

text: Make definite assertions. Avoid tame, colorless, hesitating, non-committal language.
teaches: Say what you mean without hedging: a claim the reader can act on.
avoid: The imperative of a rule book. A letter to a person states facts; it does not issue rules.

text: The proper place in the sentence for the word, or group of words, which the writer desires to make most prominent is usually the end.
teaches: Put the word that matters most at the end of the sentence.
avoid: The long subject before the verb, which is the fault the sentence warns about.

text: Say what he is proposing to say, not merely come near it.
teaches: Name the thing itself, not something close to it.
avoid: The third person of the list and its sardonic frame; the essay mocks Cooper, and a rewrite mocks no one.

text: Use the right word, not its second cousin.
teaches: Pick the exact word over a near synonym.
avoid: The joke as a device. A professional text earns trust with the exact word, not a quip about it.

text: Employ a simple and straightforward style.
avoid: Twain's dialect and his tone elsewhere in the essay; take the rule, not the voice.

text: It is attained by choice of the word that accurately and adequately expresses what the writer has in mind, and by exclusion of that which either denotes or connotes something else.
teaches: Precision comes from choosing one word and leaving out the words that suggest something else.
avoid: The Latinate doublets (accurately and adequately, denotes or connotes) and the scolding tone of the book.

text: As Quintilian puts it, the writer should so write that his reader not only may, but must, understand.
teaches: Write so the reader cannot misread you, not only so they can follow you.
avoid: The inverted, old-fashioned order (should so write) and the appeal to a classical authority.

text: A blow is not an action but an act. An action may consist of many acts.
teaches: Two short sentences that fix one distinction with a concrete case.
avoid: The blacklist habit of forbidding words; a rewrite fixes the sentence in front of it, it does not lecture.

text: I saw the justice of his remarks, and thence grew more attentive to the manner in writing, and determined to endeavor at improvement.
teaches: Take criticism of how you write as a reason to revise, and say so plainly.
avoid: Eighteenth-century diction (thence, endeavor at) and the chain of clauses joined by and.

text: This was to teach me method in the arrangement of thoughts.
teaches: Order the ideas before you write the sentences.
avoid: The period phrasing (method in the arrangement of thoughts); today it reads: put the points in order.

text: It is altogether fitting and proper that we should do this.
teaches: A short sentence after long ones gives the reader a place to stop.
avoid: The solemn register of a speech at a cemetery and the doublet fitting and proper.

text: The world will little note, nor long remember what we say here, but it can never forget what they did here.
teaches: Contrast carried by plain, short words: say against did.
avoid: The elevated, tragic tone and the inverted word order (will little note); no email speaks like this.

text: Yalta was hardly visible through the morning mist; white clouds stood motionless on the mountain-tops.
teaches: Concrete things the reader can see, with no adjective of feeling.
avoid: The landscape and the lyric mood of a story; a professional text describes the work, not the weather.

text: He was under forty, but he had a daughter already twelve years old, and two sons at school.
teaches: Facts do the describing: ages and numbers instead of judgements.
avoid: The narrator's distance and the translated rhythm of 1917 English.
